title: Rama bows to his father
hookLine: Rama rides to his coronation through cheering streets, finds his father unable to speak, and bows at his feet
carry: pitri devo bhava: a father honored like god

lines: BARDS SING AT THE KING'S DOOR.
cards: Outside the palace, nobody knows. The sun rises on the morning Ayodhya has prepared for. Vasishtha arrives with his students and the sacred waters.
The streets are full. Bards sing outside the king's door to wake him, as they do every morning. Inside, the king hasn't slept, and he can't stand up.
Two worlds, one wall, and in a moment Rama will walk from one into the other.

teach.b: The charioteer Sumantra goes in to say everything is ready. The king can barely speak. Kaikeyi answers for him: bring Rama here.

Rama rides through packed streets and hears the people as he passes: today he'll be made heir. In Kaikeyi's room he finds his father on a couch, pale, beside the queen. Rama bows at his father's feet, then at Kaikeyi's.

teach.h: THE KING SAYS ONE WORD: RAMA.
teach.b: The king manages one word, Rama, and then his eyes fill and he can't say more. Frightened, Rama turns to Kaikeyi. Have I done something wrong?
Is he ill? The king won't speak, she says, because he's afraid to tell you something unpleasant. He made me a promise.
If you'll do what he promised, I'll tell you. And Rama says something he can't take back. At my father's word I would walk into fire.
I would drink poison. Tell me what he wants. I promise to do it, and Rama doesn't say things twice.
So Kaikeyi tells him, plainly: Bharata consecrated, Rama to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years. The boons arrive in her voice, not the king's.
But go back to what Rama did first, before any of it.

teach.h: HE BOWED AT HIS FATHER'S FEET.
teach.b: He bowed at his father's feet.

teach.h: PITRI DEVO BHAVA: A FATHER HONORED LIKE GOD.
teach.b: Hindu children still learn a line from the Taittiriya Upanishad: matri devo bhava, pitri devo bhava. Let your mother be a god to you; let your father be a god to you.
It's why so many touch their parents' and grandparents' feet before an exam, a journey, a birthday, and feel a hand on their head in return: a blessing. Rama's promise comes from that same place.
It's an epic, so he takes it to the far edge. Tomorrow, we hear his answer.

how: Touching the feet of parents and elders (pranam) and receiving a hand on the head as a blessing is still common in Hindu families. Rama bows at his father's feet, then at Kaikeyi's, before he hears the news.

o: a pardon the king grants on coronation morning
Bharata crowned, Rama exiled, told to Rama by Kaikeyi
Rama's own vow to give his kingdom to the poor

p: let your father be a god to you

s: Dasharatha tells Rama the news himself
he can only say one word, Rama; Kaikeyi tells him.
Rama promises to obey before he knows what's asked
fire or poison, he says, and he doesn't say things twice.
touching an elder's feet is about being afraid of them
it's honor and love; the elder answers with a blessing, a hand on your head.

games.q: your grandmother has come to see you off before a big exam. by today's teaching, what do many Hindu kids do?
o: a quick hug and out the door.
touch her feet and receive her blessing.
ask her to pray at home instead.
games.why: pranam: touching an elder's feet, and a hand on your head in return. Rama bowed at his father's feet the morning everything changed.

practice: Many Hindus begin a big day by bowing to a parent or grandparent, or to the photo of one who has died. Bring to mind an elder who has blessed you, living or not; if your parents are complicated, choose anyone who has stood by you.
Picture bowing to them, and feel their hand rest on your head. Breathe in their blessing. Breathe out thanks.

wordCard.voice: Kaikeyi's boons, delivered. The king can only say Rama's name; Rama bows at his feet, promises before he knows, and Kaikeyi tells him herself.

orig.note: Sanskrit pratijñā: a promise, a vow. Rama gives one before he hears what it will cost.

carryVoice: Your line: pitri devo bhava: a father honored like god. Tomorrow, we hear how Rama answers. Until tomorrow.
